evidence: Facility self sign-up (D14), shipped closed, with the fixes of its adversarial review, the two read-only commands of the website's second contract and the fixes of its second review. 0086 ports main 0061-0063 (db49a0d, 46a173f, 08c906f) with this branch's adaptations, support's review and the review fixes (R1-R12), the website contract's R13 and R14 and the second review's R15-R17, listed in 0086's header and docs/MAIN_TO_NOVU_PORT.md, and runtime-grants.sql carries its grants for a later role bootstrap. What changes: identity.organization_applications gains approval_mode (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'admin_review', metadata-only) and nullable columns for support's review (self_service_reviewed_at, self_service_reviewed_by_account_id referencing auth.accounts, self_service_review_note), support's release (self_service_released_at, self_service_released_by_account_id referencing auth.accounts, self_service_release_reason), the submitting network's keyed digest (submitter_network_digest), whether it was opened without a hold (self_service_without_hold, NOT NULL DEFAULT false, metadata-only) and when support's 7-day refusal ends (self_service_refusal_ends_at, nullable), each review and release triple set together and only on an activated self-service row, the hold and refusal only on self-service rows and the refusal only on a closed one; six partial indexes; its 0046 reviewer check is replaced by main 0062's organization_applications_review_check_self_service; identity.organization_profile_completion_challenges gains activation_attempts (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 0-5), requested_administrator_name and requested_organization_type; new definer commands submit_self_service_organization_application(text,text,text,text,text,char), public_get_organization_application, public_record_organization_cac_result, begin_self_service_provider_enrollment, prepare_self_service_provider_activation, the read-only current_self_service_provider_enrollment(char) (R13: what the password step shows before the account exists, for a live session of a ready self-service application; it needs the control and locks, charges and ends nothing) and self_service_provider_code_state(text,text,text) (R14: whether start's code went out, the code still in force and the wait before a new one; it locks and changes nothing), activate_self_service_provider_enrollment (wrapper of the owner-only activate_self_service_organization_application), the owner-only lapse helper, platform.consume_self_service_cac_quota(uuid,char,integer), the owner-only issue_organization_profile_completion_code(text,text,text,uuid,char,text) (0056's code sending, for the approval mode its caller names, R17), and support's admin_list_self_service_facilities, admin_review_self_service_facility, admin_release_self_service_facility(uuid,bigint,text,boolean), admin_list_open_self_service_applications(text), admin_reject_self_service_application(uuid,bigint,text,boolean) and admin_waive_self_service_refusals(text,text,text) (R15: a rejection or release refuses the closed application's email and network for 7 days unless support lets the applicant retry, and the waiver lifts it; a lapse refuses no one, and a new application whose email or network had one for the CAC and product closed in the last 7 days is opened without a hold; R16: the open list ranks the applications that hold a CAC now first, counts them all and searches one CAC number); two new counter tables with forced RLS and no runtime privilege; five replaced functions keep their signatures, owners and grants: identity.submit_organization_application (0052's body plus the 24-hour lapse of an abandoned self-service application), identity.begin_organization_profile_completion (0056's, which now sends a code only for a governed admin_review application and answers NULL for a self-service one, as for none, R17), platform.prune_verification_quotas (0049's body plus the two new tables), platform.consume_qoreid_quota (0049's body plus a 42501 refusal of an existing_cac lookup for a self-signed-up organization support has not reviewed, CRITIC C13) and platform.control_enabled (0040's body plus the key provider_self_service_enabled); platform.control_settings's key CHECK is replaced with the six live keys plus the new one, and the new control is seeded OFF. The table has no INSERT policy, so the seed reads its FORCE row-level security setting and, only if it is on, lifts it for that one insert and restores it, as main 0098 does; a table without FORCE is left without it (R8). Nothing is dropped except the two replaced CHECK constraints; no applied migration is rewritten; no existing grant is removed. Preconditions refuse to run (in the release's dry run, so nothing changes) unless exactly one reviewer check and one control-key check exist, both control lists name exactly the six live keys, the prune deletes exactly the 0049 tables, platform.consume_qoreid_quota's body is 0049's and identity.begin_organization_profile_completion's body is 0056's (md5 of each source; the latter shown to stop the migration on a copy with another body). Proof that no existing closed application can fail the new review check: the 0046 check admits a closed row only with a reviewer and a review time and either a review reason of 8+ characters or a NULL reason (a NULL check result passes); the new check requires reviewed_at and a coalesced reason of 8+ characters and, for admin_review rows (all existing rows), a reviewer; so exactly the closed rows with a NULL review_reason pass the old check and fail the new one. Every command that closes an application writes a reason of 8+ characters, so only a direct write could leave one, and 0086 counts closed rows without a reason of 8+ characters, reviewer or review time first and raises a clear exception if any exist (shown on a copy holding one such row). Read-only preflights before signing (docs/MAIN_TO_NOVU_PORT.md lists them too): P1 select count(*) from identity.organization_applications where status in ('approved','rejected') and (review_reason is null or length(btrim(review_reason)) < 8 or reviewed_at is null or reviewed_by_account_id is null) must be 0; P2 select conrelid::regclass, conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid in ('identity.organization_applications'::regclass,'platform.control_settings'::regclass) and contype='c' must show exactly one reviewer check and one control_key check of the six keys; C2 the owner of platform.control_settings and of platform.control_enabled(text) must be the migration login (for FORCE and CREATE OR REPLACE), or the dry run stops the release with nothing changed; R8 select c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity, pg_get_userbyid(c.relowner), r.rolsuper, r.rolbypassrls from pg_class c join pg_roles r on r.oid = c.relowner where c.oid = 'platform.control_settings'::regclass: if row-level security and FORCE are both on and the owner has neither rolsuper nor rolbypassrls, stop and find out why first, since production's accountless control reads could not then work as they do; every other state is kept as it is. R17 select proc.oid::regprocedure, md5(proc.prosrc) from pg_proc proc where proc.oid in ('platform.consume_qoreid_quota(text,uuid,uuid,char,char)'::regprocedure, 'identity.begin_organization_profile_completion(text,text,text,uuid,char)'::regprocedure) must show 0049's dca2fbb737f2c747148eacc7d6e66c5f and 0056's 6c94f9fca935f41a1bbcc313d9447d04, which 0086 requires, or its dry run stops the release with nothing changed. Backward compatibility and rollback: the previous Identity (57a94db) calls none of the new commands; its governed intake still inserts admin_review rows by default; its governed approve and reject always name a reviewer and a reason of 8+ characters, which the new check admits; the replaced governed submit, prune, consume_qoreid_quota and control_enabled keep their signatures and answers for every input the previous code sends, except three that exist only once the control has been opened: the governed submit lapses a self-service row a newer Identity left unactivated for 24 hours, an organization that signed itself up gets 42501 for an organization CAC lookup until support has reviewed it (the previous Identity answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED), and the governed completion start sends no code for a self-service application (its answer stays the uniform accepted one); the admin console's control list returns seven rows, and the previous Identity's DTO cannot change the new key, which stays off. test/database/provider-self-service-rollback.integration.sql runs the previous Identity's own SQL text (governed intake, admin list, get, CAC record with the application_cac quota, approve and reject, the applicant's completion start, verify, current and complete, that start sending nothing for a self-service application with the control on and off, the existing-organization CAC binding match and its existing_cac quota for a facility that signed itself up, the control list and change, the guard's control reads, the prune) as hid_identity_api_runtime on the new schema. Gate: with the control off, submit, the activation pre-check and activation raise 55000 PLATFORM_CONTROL_DISABLED:provider_self_service_enabled and write nothing; the pre-check reads the control after locking the session; the control is read from Identity's accountless context exactly as the security guard's portal check already reads it in production; under an owner that cannot bypass row-level security, with FORCE on, the gate stays closed (55000 PLATFORM_CONTROL_UNAVAILABLE). Locks until commit, measured with pg_locks on PostgreSQL 16 on a copy of the 0085 production-order database: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.organization_applications and identity.organization_profile_completion_challenges, and SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.accounts (the reviewer and release foreign keys), from the first statements; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on platform.control_settings only in the control section, which is the last statements of the file (3.1 to 8.0 ms of 52 to 67 ms in four runs on an empty database; the read-only commands lock nothing); replacing platform.consume_qoreid_quota and identity.begin_organization_profile_completion takes no table lock. Tests: built in production order (0001-0072, role bootstrap with the 0072-era runtime-grants.sql, then 0073-0086 with apply-migrations.mjs), the same followed by a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql, and in new-installation order (0001-0086, then role bootstrap): all 43 suites pass in each (16 in services/ehr-api/database/tests, unchanged, and 27 in services/ehr-api/test/database, 10 of them new with this change); the 10 new suites fail on a database built to 0085, where the other 33 pass; the suites catch each of 23 deliberate defects in the reviewed 0086's ported part, each of 22 in R13 and R14 and their grants, each of 34 in the second review's R15-R17 and their grants, and 25 of 27 in its review fixes, the other two being caught by the runtime verifier (the pre-check reading the control before the session's lock) and by the upgrade rehearsal (a seed that turns FORCE on). Under a non-superuser NOBYPASSRLS definer owner (the rehearsal's owner swap) every new suite passes. The plan and dry run on a 0085 database list and roll back only 0086; a dry run of 0084-0086 in one transaction on a 0083 database succeeds. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs rehearses production's order as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (baseline, role bootstrap with the baseline runtime-grants.sql, dry run, migrations, then requires that a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql changes no runtime privilege), now also requires that the release change no existing table's row-level security or FORCE setting, and releases a baseline with FORCE lifted on platform.control_settings, where FORCE must stay off and the Identity runtime must still read platform.control_enabled from an accountless connection; it passes, and fails with a seed that always turns FORCE on. scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs passes; this release adds one check to it, provider_enrollment_runtime (services/identity-api/scripts/verify-provider-enrollment-runtime.mjs, the Identity runtime role end to end, including the database's own gate driven through Identity), which passes, now also proving R13's confirmation read, R14's answer when no code is sent, and the second review's fixes: the registered email closing its application and another email accepted at once from the same network, the governed completion route sending no code for a self-service application, a squatter's renewal from its own network accepted without a hold and lapsed at once by the real company, the open list's ranking, total and search, support's waiver and a retry rejection. reviewed_by is left empty for the owner.
